our_title: Empty vertex-bipartition part: recursion on part 0 without part array, and terminal target domain mishandled
ran:
Build: INFRA/asan (pristine 7.0.17, ASan+UBSan, 32-bit Gnum) vs $WORK/build (same flags, this series); LD_LIBRARY_PATH=<tree>/lib, UBSAN_OPTIONS=print_stacktrace=1, ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0 unless stated. Reproducers and exact commands in $WORK/repro/<ID>/README.
$WORK/repro/SEP-01/partovl.32 6 3 'r{sep=z}' (pristine):
  wgraph_part_rb.c:108:5: runtime error: null pointer passed as argument 2 ... #0 wgraphPartRb3Fron #1 wgraphPartRb2 wgraph_part_rb.c:299 #2 wgraphPartRb2 wgraph_part_rb.c:363
  wgraph_part_rb.c:207:18: runtime error: load of null pointer of type 'const GraphPart' ; AddressSanitizer: SEGV in wgraphPartRb3One
Same for 7/8/9 vertices x 3 parts with 'z'; 4 and 5 parts return 'ret=0 part: 0 0 0 0 0 0' (spltnum 0 with domnsiz >= 2 survives by luck). Patched: 6 3 'r{sep=z}' -> ret=0 part: 0 0 0 0 0 0; matrix of n=6..9, p=3..5, strategies z/f/h/g/default all ret=0, no sanitizer report.
One-token alternative (alt/SEP-01-a) built by symbol interposition against the pristine library: ./partovl_sep01a 6 3 'r{sep=(z|f)}' -> ret=0 part: 1 1 1 1 1 1 (every vertex in part 1 although the surviving fake part only owns domain 0); recommended fix -> 0 0 0 0 0 0.
New check line `test_scotch_graph_part_ovl 3 data/m16x16.grf /dev/null 'r{sep=z}'`: pristine library -> runtime error + SEGV (rc 141); patched -> passes.
severity_note: Public API (SCOTCH_graphPartOvl) crash in release builds; needs a bipartition that leaves a part empty, which happens on small (sub)graphs with real strategies and always with 'z'. Same rating as the review.
location_7_0_17: src/libscotch/wgraph_part_rb.c:355-368 (empty-part branch, call at :363), :297-304 (terminal-domain branch taken when spltnum == 0), :330-331 (dwgttab from inddomnsiz / 2)
upstream_change: 813ef60 (08 oct 2026) only changed the type of indvertnbr in this file (int -> Gnum); the empty-part branch is untouched.
review_accuracy: Accurate on the crash mechanism (spltnum = partval = 0, NULL parttax, uninitialised splttab[0].vertnbr). Its 'Fix:' line (call with 1) is incomplete: it stops the crash but leaves the terminal-domain case wrong (shown above with r{sep=(z|f)}). Making Rb3* return errors through revaptr is unnecessary: their only failure paths are debug-only parameter checks that cannot trigger once the call is right.
first_pass_critique: Status, method and reproducer right; the preferred option (one-token fix) was tested only with strategies for which the degenerate child bipartition happens to put everything in part 0, so the wrong-domain case was missed; option 2 (guard in callee) has the same hole and leaves the recursion bipartitioning a graph onto a single domain. The 'maintainer precedent' claimed (wgraphPartRb starts with fake part 1) supports calling with 1 but not the missing terminal case.

extra_instances.quote: if ((partval = 1, (actgrafdat.compsize0 == 0)) || ... kgraphMapRbPart2 (contptr, spltnum, spltptr); /* Run bipartitioning on same subgraph */

fix_options.label: Recurse on fake part 1 and map directly onto a terminal domain (recommended)
fix_options.summary: In the empty-part branch: if the surviving part owns a single domain, put all vertices (separator included) in part 0 with vgraphZero() and map them with wgraphPartRb3One(); otherwise call wgraphPartRb2 (contptr, 1, &spltdat) as the TRICK comment intends.
fix_options.tested: repro matrix above (32-bit and 64-bit patched builds), check_scotch_graph_part_ovl (+ new line), check_prog_gpart_overlap, SCOTCH_DEBUG_ALL build runs wgraphCheck() after it: clean.
fix_options.tradeoffs: No behaviour change when no part is empty. Reuses existing helpers; vgraphZero() costs one memset of the part array.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Mirrors the kgraph twin: kgraphMapRbPart2 handles the empty part by recursing on the same subgraph with the surviving subdomain (kgraph_map_rb_part.c:290-302) and kgraphMapRbPart3 maps a whole graph onto a terminal domain (:133-156). Same 'TRICK' reuse style as the surrounding code.

fix_options.label: One-token fix: always recurse on fake part 1
fix_options.tested: interposed into the pristine library: no crash on the matrix, but 'r{sep=(z|f)}' on 2..8 vertices x 3/7 parts maps every vertex onto the sibling's domain (part 1 1 1 ...).
fix_options.tradeoffs: Stops the crash; still bipartitions a graph onto a single domain with dwgttab {0,1} and may assign vertices outside the target range.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Too small: leaves a silent wrong result.

fix_options.label: Guard the terminal branch in the callee
fix_options.summary: Make the small-branch test `(indpartval == 0) && (orgparttax != NULL)` so a NULL part array means whole graph.
fix_options.tested: untested: same hole as option 2 (whole graph still bipartitioned onto one domain), rejected by reading.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Relies on parttax == NULL as a flag; does not fix the terminal case.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Not what the code's own comment intends.

test_added: src/check/Makefile and src/check/CMakeLists.txt: test_scotch_graph_part_ovl 3 data/m16x16.grf /dev/null 'r{sep=z}' (checks the empty-part path; crashes on pristine).
notes: The Rb3* helpers still return void with debug-only checks; acceptable since the only invalid call is removed. Commit 0007.

our_title: Overlap partition leaves separator vertices with no neighbour in any part, so they belong to no part
ran:
Build: INFRA/asan (pristine 7.0.17, ASan+UBSan, 32-bit Gnum) vs $WORK/build (same flags, this series); LD_LIBRARY_PATH=<tree>/lib, UBSAN_OPTIONS=print_stacktrace=1, ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0 unless stated. Reproducers and exact commands in $WORK/repro/<ID>/README.
$WORK/repro/SEP-17/partovl.32 2 3 - 1 (edgeless, pristine) -> ret=0 part: 2 -1 ; 3 6 - 1 -> ret=0 part: -1 -1 -1
$WORK/repro/SEP-17/lost.32 4 4 - (PATH graph, default strategy, pristine) -> ret=0 part: -1 -1 -1 3  lost=2 ; 5 5 - -> lost=1 ; 10 9 - -> lost=2
Patched: 2 3 - 1 -> ret=0 part: 2 0 ; 3 6 - 1 -> 2 1 0 ; lost.32 4 4 - -> part: -1 0 -1 3 lost=0 ; all 14 tried cases lost=0. SCOTCH_DEBUG_ALL build (wgraphCheck after the post-pass) check_scotch_graph_part_ovl and check_prog_gpart_overlap clean.
severity_note: Silent wrong result (a vertex in no part) but only on tiny (sub)graphs: isolated vertices, or pendant/boundary vertices of induced subgraphs at the leaves of the recursion; the review's Low is right. Reachable with the default strategy on ordinary graphs (path 4 vertices / 4 parts), not only on edgeless graphs.
location_7_0_17: src/libscotch/wgraph_part_rb.c:441-454 (wgraphPartRb: recursion then wgraphCost, no post-processing); vertices put in the separator by vgraph methods on induced subgraphs (vgraph_separate_gg.c:172-189 leaves the last root in the separator when balance stops the growth)
evidence: doc/src/scotch/s_l.tex:1177-1180: 'the load of every separator vertex is accounted for several times, in each of the parts it separates' -- a separator vertex with no neighbour in a part separates nothing and is counted nowhere (wgraph.c:203-221 wgraphCost adds a separator vertex's load only to neighbouring parts). wgraph_part_rb.c:449-454: grafptr->fronnbr = datadat.fronnbr; ... wgraphCost (grafptr) -- nothing removes such vertices.
review_accuracy: Behaviour accurately described but the lead only covers zero-degree vertices; the same loss happens to vertices isolated in an induced subgraph, or whose neighbours all became separator vertices at other recursion levels (path 4 vertices / 4 parts: vertices 0 and 1 are lost). Its 'Fix:' (vertex-separation strategies) is one of the options but would change nested-dissection orderings and not cover the multi-level case.
first_pass_critique: Preferred option (post-pass on zero-degree vertices only) does not fix 'path 4 4' (still lost=2, see alt/SEP-17-a); the lost condition is 'no neighbour in a part', not degree zero. Its option 2 ('assign them while gluing') is not compiled and cannot see cross-level losses. Option 3 (vgraph separators) is correctly flagged as large blast radius.

fix_options.label: Post-pass in wgraphPartRb: assign to the lightest part every separator vertex with no neighbour in a part (recommended)
fix_options.summary: New static wgraphPartRbFron() called after wgraphCost(): removes such vertices from the frontier, assigns them to the lightest part, updates compload/compsize/fronload incrementally (neighbouring separator vertices now separate that part too).
fix_options.tested: repro above; check_scotch_graph_part_ovl, check_prog_gpart_overlap on 32-bit, 64-bit and SCOTCH_DEBUG_ALL builds (wgraphCheck validates the updated loads).
fix_options.tradeoffs: Changes outputs only when lost vertices exist; O(sum of degrees of lost vertices and their neighbours). Choice of the lightest part ignores locality (a lost vertex may be far from its part); a 2-hop neighbourhood choice would be a refinement.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Local to the RB method that produces the situation, guarantees the documented model for every vertex, does not touch the vgraph separators used by orderings. Same 'fix-up after recursion' idea as kgraphMapRbVfloMerge().

fix_options.label: Post-pass on zero-degree vertices only (first pass)
fix_options.summary: Move isolated frontier vertices to the lightest part.
fix_options.tested: read and compared: misses subgraph-isolated vertices (path 4 4 keeps lost=2 on the recommended fix's test matrix reasoning: vertex 0 has degree 1).

fix_options.label: Fix at the source in vgraphSeparateGg: do not leave an isolated root in the separator
fix_options.summary: When growth stops for balance reasons and the current root has no neighbour, put it back in part 0.
fix_options.tested: untested: only one of several separator methods (FM, DF, BD, ML...), does not cover cross-level losses; changes ordering results.

test_added: none: the existing check inputs (m16x16, bump, 4-32 parts) do not produce lost vertices; a deterministic case would need a tiny graph data file (path of 4 vertices) which is not in the file's style; repro/SEP-17/lost.c is the check.
notes: Design point for the maintainer: which part a lost vertex should join (lightest part here; alternative: a part adjacent to one of its separator neighbours). Commit 0008.

our_title: Fixed-vertex merge hash table sized from load slots, not fixed vertices: infinite probe loop with zero loads
ran:
Build: INFRA/asan (pristine 7.0.17, ASan+UBSan, 32-bit Gnum) vs $WORK/build (same flags, this series); LD_LIBRARY_PATH=<tree>/lib, UBSAN_OPTIONS=print_stacktrace=1, ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0 unless stated. Reproducers and exact commands in $WORK/repro/<ID>/README.
$WORK/repro/GRA-01/gra01.32 64 1 -> ret=0 (unit loads) ; timeout 20 ./gra01.32 64 0 -> Terminated rc=124 (hang) ; also 40 0, 33 0, 32 0 hang (6 free vertices -> hashnbr 6 -> 32 slots).
Patched: 64 0 -> ret=0 100 101 ... ; 32 0 -> ret=0 ; 300 0 1 -> ret=0.
New case in test_scotch_graph_map.c (all vertices but one fixed, zero loads, distinct terminals, cmplt(vertnbr)): run against the pristine library: timeout 120 ./test_scotch_graph_map data/m4x4.grf -> rc=124 (hang); patched 32/64/debug builds: passes.
severity_note: Hang from the public API with legal input (zero-load fixed vertices are explicitly allowed: 'Vertex loads can be 0 if we have fixed vertices', library_graph_map.c:209). Same as review.
location_7_0_17: src/libscotch/kgraph_map_rb.c:409-412 (sizing), :456-473 (probe loop without exit), :291-296 (vflonbr set to 0 when all loads are zero), :393-395 (vfixnbr parameter unused)
review_accuracy: Accurate, including the regime (distinct fixed terminals > 4 x next power of two of domnnbr).
first_pass_critique: Right on status and mechanism. Its preferred one-liner (domnnbr + vfixnbr) is correct but leaves the vflonbr parameter unused instead of removing it, and does not bound the table by the architecture size as kgraphMapRbVfloBuild() does (for a fixed-size architecture with 1M fixed vertices on 4 terminals it would allocate a 64 MB table). Its option 2 would pass vflonbr > 0 with vflotab == NULL into kgraphMapRbVfloSplit(), which dereferences vflotab: a crash. The hashtab leak it notes on the mapResize path is real and is fixed by the GRA-23 commit (single exit point).

extra_instances.quote: hashsiz = 1 << (hashsiz + 2); /* Fill hash table at 25% maximum */

fix_options.label: Size from min(archsize, vfixnbr) + domnnbr, drop the vflonbr parameter (recommended)
fix_options.summary: Mirror kgraphMapRbVfloBuild()'s bound in kgraphMapRbVfloMerge(); remove the now unused vflonbr parameter from the routine, its prototype and its caller; drop the misleading 'Use fixed vertex load slots as hash slots' comment.
fix_options.tested: repro above; check_scotch_graph_map (with new case) on 32-bit, 64-bit and SCOTCH_DEBUG_ALL builds; check_scotch_graph_map_copy, check_prog_gmap.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Memory of the temporary table bounded by the architecture size for fixed-size architectures; unchanged otherwise. Internal signature change (library ABI unaffected).
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Same idiom 170 lines above (kgraph_map_rb.c:234-241); removes what becomes unused, as his commits do ('Remove useless structure definition').

fix_options.label: One-liner: hashnbr = domnnbr + vfixnbr (first pass)
fix_options.summary: Use the unused parameter as the bound; remove vflonbr.
fix_options.tested: equivalent behaviour on the repro (same loop, larger table); not built separately.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Over-allocates for many fixed vertices on few terminals.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Acceptable but less careful than his own Build routine.

fix_options.label: Bound the probe loop and fail when the table is full
fix_options.summary: Count probes; errorPrint + return 1 instead of looping.
fix_options.tested: untested: turns the hang into an error without making the input work; only useful as defence in depth.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: He does not guard hash loops elsewhere.

cleanup_done: removed the unused vflonbr parameter of kgraphMapRbVfloMerge() (kgraph_map_rb.c, kgraph_map_rb.h, caller) and a stale comment
test_added: src/check/test_scotch_graph_map.c: 'zero-load fixed vertices' block (graph copy with loads, cmplt(vertnbr), all vertices but one fixed to distinct terminals, both strategies, checkMap); hangs on pristine.
notes: The `1 << (hashsiz + 2)` int shift (extra_instances) overflows for more than 2^29 entries; unreachable in practice, listed in extra.json as PS2-G12-4. Commit 0003.

our_title: kgraphMapRbBgraph() error paths return without freeing the bipartition graph it initialised
ran:
Build: INFRA/asan (pristine 7.0.17, ASan+UBSan, 32-bit Gnum) vs $WORK/build (same flags, this series); LD_LIBRARY_PATH=<tree>/lib, UBSAN_OPTIONS=print_stacktrace=1, ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0 unless stated. Reproducers and exact commands in $WORK/repro/<ID>/README. (LeakSanitizer ON for this item)
$WORK/repro/GRA-21/gra21.32 100 c (pristine): ERROR: kgraphMapRbBgraph: invalid fixed part array / kgraphMapRbPart2: cannot create bipartition graph ; LeakSanitizer: 'Direct leak of 1016 byte(s) ... #1 _SCOTCHbgraphInit bgraph.c:120 #2 _SCOTCHkgraphMapRbBgraph kgraph_map_rb.c:530 #3 kgraphMapRbPart2 kgraph_map_rb_part.c:255'; ./gra21.32 100 h: same through kgraphMapRbMap.
Patched: no bgraphInit frame; only the reproducer's own arrays remain (5124 bytes in 2 allocations).
Allocation-failure path, plain build + LD_PRELOAD: FAIL_NTH=53 LD_PRELOAD=repro/common/failmalloc.so ./gra21.plain 1 c (patched) -> 'ERROR: kgraphMapRbBgraph: out of memory' ... ret=1, 'failmalloc: 54 malloc calls, 0 blocks never freed'.
severity_note: Leak on error paths only (invalid fixed part array from the public API in release builds, or allocation failure). Same as review.
location_7_0_17: src/libscotch/kgraph_map_rb.c:547-550 (veextax allocation failure), :613-616 (archDomTerm failure -> fail:), :667-671 (fail: frees veextax only), :681-685 (debug bgraphCheck failure)
review_accuracy: Accurate. The debug-only bgraphCheck() failure (:681-685) is a third instance it did not list.
first_pass_critique: Right; its diff matches the sketch. Its title mixes in the GRA-23 debug-only validation topic. It did not exercise the allocation-failure path (done here with LD_PRELOAD).

extra_instances.quote: if (bgraphCheck (actgrafptr) != 0) { errorPrint ("kgraphMapRbBgraph: inconsistent graph data"); return (1); }

fix_options.label: bgraphExit() in the callee on every error path after bgraphInit() (recommended)
fix_options.summary: Free the bipartition graph on the allocation failure, on the fail: path when o != 0, and on the debug check failure (veextax is then owned by the graph).
fix_options.tested: LSan runs and LD_PRELOAD injection above; check_scotch_graph_map on 32/64/debug builds.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Callers keep their current logic; no double free since bgraphExit() does not free the cloned graph arrays.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: His bgraphInit() does exactly this on its own debug failure (bgraph.c:131-134); kgraph_band.c fail: label frees what the routine created.

fix_options.label: Free in the callers
fix_options.summary: kgraphMapRbPart2: goto end1 instead of end2; kgraphMapRbMap: bgraphExit() before PoolExit().
fix_options.tested: untested: rejected by reading (the callers cannot tell whether bgraphInit() succeeded; bgraphExit() on an uninitialised Bgraph reads garbage pointers).
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Ownership belongs to the routine that initialised the graph.

test_added: none: leak detection needs a sanitizer; repro/GRA-21 covers both paths
notes: PT-Scotch twin kdgraph_map_rb_part.c:383-397 already calls bdgraphExit() on failure. Commit 0004.

our_title: Invalid terminal numbers in old or fixed part arrays accepted: uninitialised domains, success returned
ran:
Build: INFRA/asan (pristine 7.0.17, ASan+UBSan, 32-bit Gnum) vs $WORK/build (same flags, this series); LD_LIBRARY_PATH=<tree>/lib, UBSAN_OPTIONS=print_stacktrace=1, ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0 unless stated. Reproducers and exact commands in $WORK/repro/<ID>/README.
$WORK/repro/GRA-23/gra23.32 100 (remap, old part 100 on cmplt(4), pristine) -> ret=0 new[7]=1 (silent)
$WORK/repro/GRA-23/gra23b.32 100 (isolated fixed vertex on terminal 100, pristine) -> kgraph_cost.c:178:34: runtime error: signed integer overflow: 1 - -2147483648 ... #1 kgraphMapRb kgraph_map_rb.c:176 ; ret=0 p[16]=0
Patched: gra23 100 -> ERROR: mapBuild3: invalid terminal array / kgraphInit: cannot initialize remapping (2) ; ret=1 ; gra23b 100 -> ERROR: kgraphMapRbVfloMerge: invalid fixed part array / kgraphMapRb: cannot merge fixed vertex domains ; ret=1 ; valid inputs unchanged (ret=0).
Behaviour change observed: gpart 16 data/bump_imbal_32.grf /dev/null -rodata/bump_old.map (32 old parts onto a 16-terminal architecture) is now rejected with 'mapBuild3: invalid terminal array'; it previously computed on uninitialised domains.
severity_note: Higher than the review's Low: reachable from the public API in release builds (validation is SCOTCH_DEBUG_LIBRARY1 only), produces UB in cost computation and a success code; the gpart case shows users can hit it by remapping onto fewer parts.
location_7_0_17: src/libscotch/mapping.c:389 (mapBuild3); src/libscotch/kgraph_map_rb.c:466 (kgraphMapRbVfloMerge); related debug-only check src/libscotch/kgraph_map_rb.c:344-355 (kgraphMapRbVfloSplit)
evidence:
mapping.c:389: archDomTerm (archptr, &domntab[domnnbr], termnum); /* Create slot with terminal number domain */
kgraph_map_rb.c:466: archDomTerm (archptr, &mappptr->domntab[domnnum], pfixval); /* Add new domain to domain array */
kgraph_map_rb.c:613-616 (same input, checked): if (archDomTerm (archptr, &domndat, pfixval) != 0) { errorPrint ("kgraphMapRbBgraph: invalid fixed part array"); goto fail; }
library_graph_map.c:197-205 and :238-244: the checks of parotab / fixed parttab are under #ifdef SCOTCH_DEBUG_LIBRARY1.
review_accuracy: Accurate; the fix line is what was implemented. It did not mention that kgraphMapRbVfloMerge() also leaked its hash table on its mapResize() failure path, fixed in the same restructuring.
first_pass_critique: Right. Its diff for Merge set domnnbr and freed hashtab inline at one site only; the maintainer's idiom in the sibling routine mapBuild3() (o / fail: / memFree) covers all four error paths, which is what the patch does. Its option 2 (unconditional validation at the API boundary) is a valid alternative, tested here as alt/GRA-23-b.

extra_instances.quote: archDomTerm (archptr, &domndat, vflotab[vflonum].termnum); #ifdef SCOTCH_DEBUG_KGRAPH2 if (o != 0) { errorPrint ("kgraphMapRbVfloSplit: internal error"); return; }
archDomTerm (archptr, &domndat, tgtnum); /* Get weight of terminal domain */

fix_options.label: Check archDomTerm() in mapBuild3() and kgraphMapRbVfloMerge(), single exit point in Merge (recommended)
fix_options.summary: goto fail with 'invalid terminal array' / 'invalid fixed part array'; Merge gets the o/fail: structure of mapBuild3() so that the hash table is freed on every error (mapResize failure included).
fix_options.tested: repro above; check_scotch_graph_map, check_scotch_graph_map_copy, check_prog_gpart_remap, check_prog_gmap on 32/64/debug builds.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Invalid input now fails instead of computing on garbage (remapping from a mapping onto a larger architecture is rejected, consistent with the debug-mode check 'invalid old partition').
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Same check and message he wrote at kgraph_map_rb.c:613-616; error-path structure copied from mapBuild3() (mapping.c:359-404).

fix_options.label: Validate the part arrays unconditionally at the library boundary
fix_options.summary: Move the SCOTCH_DEBUG_LIBRARY1 loops of graphMapCompute2() out of the #ifdef.
fix_options.tested: untested as a build; read: O(n) archDomTerm calls per API call, covers Split too, but leaves mapBuild3() (used for user-provided old mappings) and Merge trusting their input.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Defence at one place only; he put the SCOTCH_dgraphRedist() parameter check under SCOTCH_DEBUG_LIBRARY1 in 7.0.17 (b10825d), so he may not want unconditional API checks.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Possible complement, not his first choice.

test_added: none: an invalid-input test would need a new error-expecting harness; repro/GRA-23 covers both routines
notes: kgraphMapRbVfloSplit() still trusts its terminal numbers (debug check only); it runs before Merge, so with the patch an invalid fixed terminal with non-zero load is still used in archDomIncl() on an uninitialised domain inside Split before being rejected by Bgraph/Merge; making Split return int would change two callers (kgraph_map_rb_part.c:253, kgraph_map_rb_map.c:942). The library_graph_map_view.c / library_dgraph_map_stat.c instances belong to the API groups. Commit 0005.
